key_insight: FrontierPhysics moves beyond isolated physics questions toward evaluating AI agents on end-to-end research. It introduces 56 tasks created by 42 physicists from their own research, spanning nine physics domains.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks focus on fixed questions, isolated subtasks, or reproducing papers with known solutions, leaving gaps in assessing broader research capability and research quality alongside correctness.
method: Build a benchmark from 56 research-grounded tasks contributed by 42 physicists.
Cover nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics.
Target end-to-end research evaluation rather than isolated problem solving; the supplied abstract is truncated and does not specify the full workflow or scoring criteria.
impact: FrontierPhysics offers AI/ML practitioners a broader testbed for developing physics research agents. It emphasizes that useful scientific AI must demonstrate research quality, not just correct answers.
visual_elements: Three headline counters: 56 tasks, 42 physicists, nine domains.
A three-branch diagram showing theoretical, computational, and experimental physics.
A comparison graphic contrasting isolated benchmark questions with end-to-end research tasks.
Paired evaluation icons highlighting correctness and research quality.
paper_title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
paper_authors: Bingran You, Wenjun Ke, Ria Rosenauer, Bo Liu, Wenbo Chen
